name: NEPTUNE
aliases: Solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS fixed-dose combination
question: Does fixed-dose solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS improve storage and voiding symptoms more than tamsulosin OCAS or placebo in men with lower urinary tract symptoms?

arms.label: Solifenacin 6 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg daily
solifenacin 9 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg daily

design.population: 1,334 men with moderate-to-severe storage and voiding lower urinary tract symptoms, total IPSS at least 13, maximum flow 4–12 mL/s, at least two severe urgency episodes and eight micturitions daily, prostate volume under 75 mL, and postvoid residual at most 150 mL.
design.locator: van Kerrebroeck 2013, PubMed abstract, Methods; Drake 2015, PDF p2, Methods; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01018511, Participant Flow, Started

verdictNote: The 6 mg combination met all success criteria; the 9 mg combination did not.
takeaway: Over 12 weeks, fixed-dose solifenacin 6 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS met prespecified IPSS and urgency-frequency criteria versus placebo and tamsulosin OCAS alone; the 9 mg solifenacin combination did not meet all criteria versus tamsulosin.

reports.label: Primary 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: van Kerrebroeck P, Chapple C, Drogendijk T, et al. "Combination Therapy with Solifenacin and Tamsulosin Oral Controlled Absorption System in a Single Tablet for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men: Efficacy and Safety Results from the Randomised Controlled NEPTUNE Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(6):1003-1012. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.07.034

results.measure: Mean change in total IPSS at 12 weeks; 6 mg combination versus tamsulosin and placebo
results.note: Prespecified success required superiority to placebo and noninferiority to tamsulosin for total IPSS; the abstract reports the 6 mg combination met all criteria but gives no margin or interval.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Outcome Measurements and Results

results.endpoint: Total Urgency and Frequency Score, 6 mg combination
results.measure: Mean change in TUFS at 12 weeks; 6 mg combination versus tamsulosin and placebo
results.note: Prespecified success required superiority to tamsulosin for TUFS; the abstract reports all 6 mg combination criteria met without an effect interval.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Outcome Measurements and Results

results.endpoint: Joint primary success criteria, 9 mg combination
results.measure: Mean change in total IPSS and TUFS at 12 weeks
results.note: The abstract says the 9 mg combination met criteria versus placebo but not versus tamsulosin; it does not specify the failed contrast or margin.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Outcome Measurements and Results

delivery.label: Randomized regimen
delivery.value: Once-daily placebo, tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg, or a single fixed-dose tablet combining tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg with solifenacin 6 or 9 mg for 12 weeks.

reports.label: NEPTUNE II open-label extension
reports.citation: Drake MJ, Chapple C, Sokol R, et al. "Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Single-tablet Combinations of Solifenacin and Tamsulosin Oral Controlled Absorption System in Men with Storage and Voiding Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: Results from the NEPTUNE Study and NEPTUNE II Open-label Extension." *Eur Urol.* 2015;67(2):262-270. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2014.07.013
reports.followUp: 40-week open-label extension after 12-week NEPTUNE; up to 52 weeks of fixed-dose combination exposure

results.measure: Mean change from original NEPTUNE baseline to end of treatment, up to 52 weeks
results.note: Pooled flexible-dose extension; no concurrent randomized comparator.

results.measure: Mean change from original NEPTUNE baseline to end of treatment, up to 52 weeks
results.note: Pooled flexible-dose extension; no concurrent randomized comparator.

harms.label: Treatment-emergent adverse events
harms.note: Events during fixed-dose combination exposure in NEPTUNE or NEPTUNE II among extension participants.

harms.label: Dry mouth and constipation
harms.note: Extension safety population; treatment-emergent events during fixed-dose combination exposure.

harms.label: Adverse-event discontinuation
harms.note: Discontinuation owing to adverse events in the extension safety population.

delivery.label: Extension dosing
delivery.value: All extension participants started four weeks of solifenacin 6 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg daily, then could choose 6 or 9 mg solifenacin and switch at later 12-week visits.

delivery.label: Extension completion
delivery.value: 1,066/1,199 NEPTUNE completers received an extension dose; 960/1,066 (90.1%) completed NEPTUNE II.

reports.label: Responder and quality-of-life analysis
reports.citation: Drake MJ, Sokol R, Coyne K, et al. "Responder and Health-related Quality of Life Analyses in Men with Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms Treated with a Fixed-dose Combination of Solifenacin and Tamsulosin Oral-controlled Absorption System: Results from the NEPTUNE Study." *BJU Int.* 2016;117(1):165-172. doi:10.1111/bju.13162
reports.followUp: 12-week randomized treatment, secondary responder and quality-of-life analysis

results.measure: Number of responder analyses favoring the 6 mg combination at 12 weeks
results.note: Counts are analyses, not patients; the abstract does not give patient-level response denominators.

reports.label: Urinary-retention subanalysis
reports.citation: Drake MJ, Oelke M, Snijder R, et al. "Incidence of Urinary Retention during Treatment with Single Tablet Combinations of Solifenacin+tamsulosin OCAS for up to 1 Year in Adult Men with Both Storage and Voiding LUTS: A Subanalysis of the NEPTUNE/NEPTUNE II Randomized Controlled Studies." *PLoS One.* 2017;12(2):e0170726. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0170726
reports.followUp: Up to 52 weeks of fixed-dose combination exposure across NEPTUNE and NEPTUNE II

harms.label: Urinary retention during randomized treatment
harms.note: Safety denominators; tamsulosin case was acute urinary retention. No placebo-arm randomized-treatment count is reported in Table 1.

harms.label: Catheter-requiring acute urinary retention during randomized treatment
harms.note: AUR was the subset of urinary retention requiring catheterization.

harms.label: Urinary retention during combined follow-up
harms.note: Any fixed-dose combination exposure in either study; no concurrent control across this follow-up.

harms.label: Catheter-requiring retention during combined follow-up
harms.note: Acute urinary retention over up to 52 weeks of fixed-dose combination exposure.
